originNotListening.detail: Start the app this route sends traffic to; visitors see an error until it runs.

noConnections.title: This Mac's connector isn't running
noConnections.detail: Its routes don't answer until the connector runs.

crashLoop.title: This Mac's connector keeps stopping
crashLoop.detail: cloudflared exited several times in a row. Its logs say why; starting it again retries.

degraded.title: This Mac's connector lost its connection
degraded.detail: cloudflared is running but not connected to Cloudflare. It reconnects on its own; check the network if it persists.
degraded.title@windows: This PC's connector lost its connection
degraded.title@linux: This computer's connector lost its connection

staleConnections.title: Cloudflare still lists connections for this Mac's tunnel
staleConnections.detail: This Mac's connector isn't running, so they're left over, or another machine runs this tunnel with its token. Clean them up if nothing else should run it.
staleConnections.title@windows: Cloudflare still lists connections for this PC's tunnel
staleConnections.title@linux: Cloudflare still lists connections for this computer's tunnel
staleConnections.detail@windows: This PC's connector isn't running, so they're left over, or another machine runs this tunnel with its token. Clean them up if nothing else should run it.
staleConnections.detail@linux: This computer's connector isn't running, so they're left over, or another machine runs this tunnel with its token. Clean them up if nothing else should run it.

otherConnectors.title: Another machine also runs this Mac's tunnel
otherConnectors.detail: Cloudflare splits requests between the machines running a tunnel, and each sends them to its own services, so some visitors reach the other machine instead of this Mac. Stop cloudflared there (see its logs in Tunnels to find it), or rotate the tunnel's token by deleting and re-adding the routes.
otherConnectors.title@windows: Another machine also runs this PC's tunnel
otherConnectors.title@linux: Another machine also runs this computer's tunnel
otherConnectors.detail@windows: Cloudflare splits requests between the machines running a tunnel, and each sends them to its own services, so some visitors reach the other machine instead of this PC. Stop cloudflared there (see its logs in Tunnels to find it), or rotate the tunnel's token by deleting and re-adding the routes.
otherConnectors.detail@linux: Cloudflare splits requests between the machines running a tunnel, and each sends them to its own services, so some visitors reach the other machine instead of this computer. Stop cloudflared there (see its logs in Tunnels to find it), or rotate the tunnel's token by deleting and re-adding the routes.

duplicateLocal.title: Another cloudflared on this Mac runs this Mac's tunnel
duplicateLocal.detail: Two connectors on one Mac add nothing but confusion in logs and metrics. Stop the other one from Tunnels.
duplicateLocal.title@windows: Another cloudflared on this PC runs this PC's tunnel
duplicateLocal.title@linux: Another cloudflared on this computer runs this computer's tunnel
duplicateLocal.detail@windows: Two connectors on one PC add nothing but confusion in logs and metrics. Stop the other one from Tunnels.
duplicateLocal.detail@linux: Two connectors on one computer add nothing but confusion in logs and metrics. Stop the other one from Tunnels.

unusedOwned.title: This Mac's tunnel has no routes
unusedOwned.detail: It's kept so adding a route is quick. Delete it if you don't need it.
unusedOwned.title@windows: This PC's tunnel has no routes
unusedOwned.title@linux: This computer's tunnel has no routes

orphanRoute.title: {hostname} points at this Mac's tunnel but has no route
orphanRoute.detail: Visitors get a 404 from the tunnel. Delete the record, or add a route for it.
orphanRoute.title@windows: {hostname} points at this PC's tunnel but has no route
orphanRoute.title@linux: {hostname} points at this computer's tunnel but has no route

orphanTunnel.title: {hostname} points at a tunnel that no longer exists
orphanTunnel.detail: The hostname shows a Cloudflare error. Delete the record, or route it to a tunnel.

proxyOff.title: WARP clients can't reach private networks
proxyOff.detail: Gateway's proxy is off, so WARP clients don't send traffic for private networks through Cloudflare. In the Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard, turn on the Gateway proxy for TCP (and UDP, for services that use it) in the network settings.
proxyOff.subject: Private networks

networkExcluded.title: WARP clients don't send {network} to this Mac
networkExcluded.detail: The default device profile's Split Tunnels exclude these addresses, so WARP clients send traffic for {network} to their own network instead of this Mac. In the Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard, remove the entry from Split Tunnels (or narrow it so it no longer covers {network}).
networkExcluded.title@windows: WARP clients don't send {network} to this PC
networkExcluded.title@linux: WARP clients don't send {network} to this computer
networkExcluded.detail@windows: The default device profile's Split Tunnels exclude these addresses, so WARP clients send traffic for {network} to their own network instead of this PC. In the Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard, remove the entry from Split Tunnels (or narrow it so it no longer covers {network}).
networkExcluded.detail@linux: The default device profile's Split Tunnels exclude these addresses, so WARP clients send traffic for {network} to their own network instead of this computer. In the Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard, remove the entry from Split Tunnels (or narrow it so it no longer covers {network}).

networkNotIncluded.title: WARP clients don't send {network} to this Mac
networkNotIncluded.detail: The default device profile's Split Tunnels only send the listed addresses through WARP, and {network} isn't one of them. In the Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard, add {network} to Split Tunnels.
networkNotIncluded.title@windows: WARP clients don't send {network} to this PC
networkNotIncluded.title@linux: WARP clients don't send {network} to this computer

accessOrphan.title: {domain} still has a login but no route
accessOrphan.detail: Teitunnel added this login for a route that was removed outside Teitunnel. It protects nothing now, but would ask for a login if the hostname is routed again elsewhere. Remove it, or add the route back.

permissionFix.title_one: The token needs one more permission
permissionFix.tunnelsWhy: To create the tunnel and serve routes through it.
permissionFix.dnsWhy: To add the route's DNS record on {zone}. Include {zone} under Zone Resources.
permissionFix.anyDnsWhy: To add routes' DNS records. Include your domains under Zone Resources.
permissionFix.accessApps: Account · Access: Apps and Policies · Edit
permissionFix.accessAppsWhy: To put a login in front of a route.
permissionFix.accessOrg: Account · Access: Organizations, Identity Providers, and Groups · Edit
permissionFix.accessOrgWhy: To add the one-time code login method when the account has none.
permissionFix.editDetail: Add them to this account's API token in Cloudflare. The token itself stays the same, so there's nothing to paste.
permissionFix.step1: Choose Edit next to the token you connected (Cloudflare names it “Teitunnel” if you used the link).
permissionFix.step2: Add the permissions above, and check that this account and your domains are included under the resources.
permissionFix.step3: Choose Continue to Summary, then Update Token.
permissionFix.autoCheck: Teitunnel checks again when you come back.
permissionFix.stillMissing: The token still lacks some of them. Check the permissions and that this account and domain are included.
permissionFix.newTokenDetail: Create a token with every permission Teitunnel uses, then paste it here. It replaces this account's current credential.
permissionFix.otherDetail: This account is connected with a login whose permissions can't be changed. Connect it with an API token instead; it replaces the current credential.
permissionFix.lbPools: Account · Load Balancing: Monitors and Pools · Edit
permissionFix.lbWhy: To load balance a route. Load Balancing is a paid Cloudflare add-on: turn it on in the dashboard first.

zeroTrustFix.title: Set up Cloudflare Zero Trust
zeroTrustFix.detail: Logins use Cloudflare Zero Trust, which is free for up to 50 users. The account hasn't used it yet, and only the dashboard can set it up.
zeroTrustFix.step1: Open Zero Trust and choose a team name.
zeroTrustFix.step2: Pick the Free plan when asked, then come back.
